title: Capacity Brokerage: Escrowed Throughput Offers, Delegated Approvals, and Autoscale Templates
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Sales and Platform teams need a more flexible path to grant customers throughput guarantees without over-provisioning fleet or requiring long procurement cycles. Current intake is monolithic (full reservation or nothing), which causes friction and manual back-and-forth for partial guarantees, burst windows, and short-term trials.

Proposal summary: Build a Capacity Brokerage flow that introduces the concept of escrowed throughput offers and delegated approval lanes. Key components: 1) Request API + UI to submit desired baseline throughput, burst credits, and time window; 2) Escrowed offers (soft guarantee) that reserve capacity for a configurable window (e.g., 7/30/90 days) with automatic reconciliation; 3) Delegated approver roles (Solutions Eng / Sales Engineering / Platform AGS) to speed approvals for low-risk requests; 4) Autoscale policy templates that map requested throughput to fleet-level min/max and burst_credit settings; 5) A forecasting/ledger view that shows 13-week rolling utilization and backlog impact; 6) Safety hedges (SLO buffer, canary routing, auto-fallback to best-effort hosted pool).

Non-goals: Not replacing full committed reservations or long-term contracts. Not implementing billing contract negotiation flows (handled by Finance).

Acceptance criteria: - Request UI and API for submitting offers (fields: desired RPS/seq, baseline tokens/min, burst_credits, reserve_window). - Broker engine prototype that can emit an "escrowed offer" object and decrement fleet available capacity in planner. - 3 autoscale policy templates (small/medium/large) that produce recommended min_capacity, max_capacity, burst_credit, and smoothing parameters. - Delegated approval ribbon in Console with TTL-based approvals (expires after configured window). - Forecast ledger mock with 13-week horizon; simulation runner that can show impact of accepting an offer on 95th percentile latency and cost. - Playbook doc for operators describing handoff steps and emergency decommit.

Design notes: We intentionally separate escrowed offers from committed reservations. Escrowed offers should be revocable if demand or failures require decommit in <48 hours with automated customer notification. Delegated approvers are scoped by impact (<=10% fleet, <=X tokens/min, <=30 days) to avoid legal/finance escalation. Autoscale templates should be idempotent and composable with existing per-customer autoscale policies.

APIs (draft): POST /broker/requests {customer_id, baseline_tokens_per_min, burst_credits, reserve_window_days, escalation_tier} GET /broker/offers/:id PATCH /broker/offers/:id/accept POST /broker/simulate {offer_spec, horizon_weeks=13}
comments: 2025-02-19 - Maya Chen: Kickoff review with Eng (R. Gomez) and SRE (L. Ibrahim). Agreed to prioritize the broker API and autoscale templates for the first sprint. Action: ENG to spike allocation model (ENG-18422).

2025-02-25 - Rahul Gomez (Eng): Spike complete. Preliminary allocator reduces headroom by escrowed_offer.amount and recomputes headroom per-az. Found edge case when multiple overlapping escrow windows exceed burst capacity; recommended soft-fail policy and queued reconciliation. Added PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/536
2025-03-03 - Product review: Decided delegated approvals should be TTL-based (24/72 hours) and limited to impact thresholds. Security flagged audit log requirement for delegated approvers (SEC-118).

2025-03-06 - Arjun Patel: UX draft uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.internal.redwood.com/display/DC/Capacity+Brokerage+UI+Draft. Includes request flow and approver ribbon. Need Design review (DES-4121).

2025-03-09 - Solutions Eng feedback (Nora Alvarez): Recommend adding a trial-style 14-day soft-guarantee template with automated conversion prompts and prefilled contract checklist for Sales. Added label: sales-concierge.

2025-03-11 - Engineering: Simulation runner shows worst-case 95th latency increase of 6% at peak if three concurrent large offers accepted; suggests per-tenant canaries and auto-fallback to hosted pool. See simulation dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.com/sim/BRK-920481

Implement broker request API and UI stub (week 1-2)
Add audit logging hooks for delegated approvals (SEC) (week 2)
Run 3 simulation scenarios and present SLO impact to SRE (week 2)
